lines: The Knight Science Journalism Fellowship Program 2020-21

The Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) invites applications for the Knight Science Journalism Fellowship Program 2020-21 from full-time journalists. This fellowship aims to support a global community of dedicated and thoughtful journalists specializing in science, technology, health and environmental reporting. Selected fellows will receive a stipend of USD 70,000, a relocation allowance of USD 2,500, and other benefits.
Be full-time journalists, whether on staff or freelance (
: Part-time writers or producers are not eligible)
Have at least three full years of experience covering science, technology, environment, or medicine
Be reporters, writers, editors, producers, illustrators, filmmakers, or photojournalists (
: This includes work for newspapers, magazines, television, radio, and digital media)
Other benefits, including basic health insurance for each fellow and their family
Follow the steps below to apply for the scholarship:
: Make login and fill the required details.
A total of 10 fellows will be selected under this program. Selections will be based on applications and video Skype interviews by a panel of distinguished science journalists.
Recipients must reside full-time in the Boston/Cambridge area for the MIT academic year, August 15th, 2020 through May 31st, 2021.
Recipients must attend field trips, seminars, and required training sessions arranged by the Knight Science Journalism Fellowship Program.
Recipients must develop a course of study that includes at least one science course per semester.
Recipients must refrain from outside professional work during the Fellowship unless written permission has been granted by the director.

Recipients must produce a well-thought-out research project during the academic year. The research project may be a book proposal, but fellows may not sell the proposal during the fellowship year, nor may they arrive with a contract to write a book during the fellowship year.

International candidates who are selected for the fellowship must obtain a valid visa from the U.S. State Department; the visa is normally sponsored by MIT. A language proficiency test (such as TOEFL) may be required as part of the visa process.
